title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors, officers, employees and their respective associates
tiers.description: The general group bound by the insider trading prohibition in section 1; broader than Key Management Personnel, who alone are subject to the trading window, blackout period, margin lending and notification rules.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Directors, Executives and their respective associates; subject to the trading window, blackout period, margin lending clearance and 3-day post-trade notification rules.

tiers.name: Chairman of the Board
tiers.description: Distinguished only for approval routing: must inform and receive written approval from the Chief Executive Officer and the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Chief Executive Officer
tiers.description: Distinguished only for approval routing: must inform and receive written approval from the Chairman and the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: other Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Distinguished only for approval routing: must inform and receive written approval from the Chairman of the Board and the Chief Executive Officer.

rules.detail: 'Securities' expressly includes derivative products, so an OTC put or call is a Security and dealing in it falls under the same trading-window regime as ordinary shares: permitted within the 30-day open windows if no inside information is held, otherwise requiring case-by-case Chairman/CEO/Company Secretary approval (or hardship approval in a blackout period).
rules.evidence: Insider trading means the buying and selling of shares, other securities, derivative products or other price sensitive products (Securities) on the basis of price-sensitive information that is not generally available to others.

rules.detail: Hedging is not named or defined anywhere in the Policy, and there is no equity incentive plan referenced with unvested holdings. A collar is a dealing in 'derivative products' and so is governed by the same trading-window/approval structure as any other dealing in Securities.

Monetisation instruments are not named; as an 'other price sensitive product' or agreement to sell Securities, monetisation would be caught by the same trading window/approval regime as ordinary dealing.

Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy. A short sale would be 'selling Securities' and so is caught by the general trading window/approval structure; there is no dedicated short-selling prohibition or disclosure rule.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are not named; as an 'other price sensitive product' referable to Hansen, dealing in a CFD would be caught by the same trading window/approval regime as ordinary Securities dealing.

Entering a margin lending arrangement, transferring Securities into an existing margin loan account, and selling Securities to satisfy a margin call are all expressly treated as dealings requiring clearance via the role-based approval procedure; approved arrangements may also be disclosed to the ASX.
rules.evidence: Any dealing in Hansen's Securities by Key Management Personnel pursuant to a margin lending arrangement must be conducted in accordance with this policy. Such dealings would include: (a) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Securities; (b) transferring Securities into an existing margin loan account; and (c) selling Securities to satisfy a call pursuant to a margin loan.

rules.detail: Entering into a margin lending arrangement (i.e. granting security over Securities) is expressly a dealing requiring clearance; more broadly, entering into any agreement giving a lender rights over a KMP's Securities triggers case-by-case Board assessment of which rules apply.
rules.evidence: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Securities

rules.detail: Not limited to margin loans: a margin lending arrangement is given only 'for example' of a secured lending arrangement. Entering into agreements that provide any lender with rights over a KMP's interests in Securities is expressly addressed, with the Board assessing applicable rules on a case-by-case basis, and a resulting forced disposal may be excluded from the Policy at the Board's discretion.
rules.evidence: a disposal of Hansen's securities on a case by case basis, that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement. On a case by case basis the Board will assess the rules that are applicable to key management personnel with respect to entering into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in Hansen's Securities.

rules.detail: No minimum holding period, LIFO rule, or intention-based short-term dealing restriction is stated.

financing_disclosure: Key Management Personnel; trigger: approval given for entry into a margin lending arrangement (inception); to: ASX, where appropriate or required by law; deadline: not specified

exemption_authority: The Board may exclude particular trades from the Policy (section 5), including case-by-case exclusion of a forced disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights over a KMP's Securities. Blackout-period trading requires Chairman/CEO/Company Secretary approval limited to severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances assessed against ASX Guidance Note 27 paragraph 11.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Hansen's securities on a case by case basis, that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement. On a case by case basis the Board will assess the rules that are applicable to key management personnel with respect to entering into agreements that provide lenders with rights over their interests in Hansen's Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy contemplates secured lending arrangements broader than margin loans and gives the Board case-by-case discretion over the rules that apply, so a bank collar with a security interest over the shares could be assessed and potentially accommodated by the Board rather than being an outright prohibition, but there is no pre-set approval path or criteria.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Should approval be given for entry into a margin lending arrangement Hansen may, where appropriate or required by law, disclose to the ASX the fact and nature of the margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar structured with a secured loan analogous to a margin lending arrangement could result in public ASX disclosure of the fact and nature of the financing at Hansen's discretion.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no hedging or equity plan concept
bespoke_clauses.clause: Insider trading means the buying and selling of shares, other securities, derivative products or other price sensitive products (Securities) on the basis of price-sensitive information that is not generally available to others.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The 2010-vintage Policy predates any specific hedging prohibition or reference to an executive equity incentive plan (only a passing reference to 'employee incentive scheme' options in section 5(g)), so a collar over vested shares is assessed purely as an ordinary dealing in Securities, not against a hedging or unvested-security rule.
The policy is dated 2010 and may have been superseded by a later, unlodged version; the terms above should be confirmed as current before relying on them for the transaction.

summary: A funded collar appears possible for Hansen Key Management Personnel, though the 2010 Policy is thin and largely silent on derivatives, hedging and short selling by name, relying instead on the broad 'Securities' definition (which expressly includes derivative products) to sweep both collar legs into the ordinary trading-window regime. Both legs could be dealt with in the open 30-day windows following half-year results, full-year results or the AGM if no inside information is held, or otherwise with case-by-case written approval from the Chairman, CEO and Company Secretary (roles cross-approving each other). The loan leg is more favourable than in many peer policies: margin lending arrangements are expressly permitted with the same role-based clearance, and section 5(f) goes further, giving the Board case-by-case discretion over which rules apply to any arrangement giving a lender rights over a KMP's Securities, so a bank-secured loan could potentially be accommodated rather than banned outright. All Key Management Personnel dealings, including under a margin/secured facility, must still be reported to the Company Secretary within 3 days, and a margin lending arrangement may be disclosed to the ASX at Hansen's discretion. Given the policy's age and silence on many collar-specific mechanics (no MSR, no vesting concept, no explicit hedging or short-selling rule), Board-level confirmation of current practice is advisable before relying on this text.
